data.answer: Whatnot announced it raised $545 million in a Series G funding round, boosting its valuation to $20 billion. The company reported live sales on its platform exceeded $8 billion in 2025, more than double the previous year, with over 20 million accounts created during the year. The number of sellers who have surpassed $1 million in lifetime sales has more than doubled over the past year, while the share of sellers earning a full-time income through the platform has risen by 25%. The funding round was co-led by ICONIQ, Lightspeed, and Avra, with participation from Kleiner Perkins, Robinhood, and Standard Capital, alongside returning backers such as Bond Capital, CapitalG, Durable Capital Partners, DST Global, and Greycroft. Whatnot's co-founders, Grant LaFontaine and Logan Head, are now each worth $2.8 billion.

The funding round was co-led by ICONIQ, Lightspeed and avra. [...] Other participants included Kleiner Perkins, Robinhood, and Standard Capital, alongside returning backers such as Bond Capital, CapitalG, Durable Capital Partners, DST Global, and Greycroft.

Whatnot is a livestream shopping platform operating in the US, UK and Europe, where users buy and sell items across categories including sneakers, trading cards, vintage fashion, jewellery, collectibles and electronics.

results.title: Whatnot valued at $20 billion as live shopping continues to boom
results.content:
Building on the growing popularity of livestreamed shopping, startup market Whatnot said on Friday that it has closed its latest round of funding at a $20 billion valuation, nearly doubling its valuation from less than a year ago.

Whatnot, which said that it has more than 650,000 new people joining its platform each week, said in a release that it had already passed the $8 billion in gross merchandise volume it saw last year. Buyers have also more than doubled over the past year. [...] Whatnot, which ranked No. 8 on this year's CNBC Disruptor 50 list, raised a $225 million Series F round led by DST Global and CapitalG in October 2025, valuing it at $11.5 billion. In January 2025, it raised $265 million in a Series E round, valuing it at nearly $5 billion. The company has raised approximately $1.5 billion since its founding in 2019.

## More coverage of the 2026 CNBC Disruptor 50 [...] With the funding from this latest round, a $545 million Series G led by Iconiq, Lightspeed and Avra, the company plans to invest in ways for sellers to grow on the platform, according to Grant LaFontaine, co-founder and CEO of Whatnot.
